notes.trap: With default settings (ANSI off, `spark.sql.legacy.sizeOfNull`=true), `size(...)` returns -1 for a NULL array or map, not NULL. Filters such as `size(col) > 0` still exclude NULLs, but `size(col) < 1` or sums of sizes silently include the -1.
`cardinality(...)` is an alias of `size(...)`, not of `array_size(...)`. With default settings it returns -1 for NULL input, unlike the standard SQL / Trino behaviour of returning NULL.

Unlike `size(...)` and `cardinality(...)`, `array_size(...)` returns NULL for NULL input regardless of `spark.sql.legacy.sizeOfNull`. It only accepts arrays, not maps, so swapping it in for `size(...)` changes both results and accepted types.

`concat(...)` returns NULL if any argument is NULL, for both strings and arrays. It does not skip NULLs or treat them as empty the way `concat_ws(...)` does. Wrap nullable inputs in `coalesce(...)` to keep the other parts.

`reverse(...)` accepts a string or an array. With ANSI off, a numeric argument is implicitly cast to STRING and reversed character by character, so a trailing zero becomes a leading zero in a string result instead of raising an error.
